Nonlinear Count Persistence and Multiple-Frequency Spatial Response

Updated October 18, 2026

This calculation retains its stated assumptions and action. For the current ten-space-plus-time physical picture, common-frequency portions and later developments, see the new particle-geometry and sector-depths case.

Current interpretation. This article preserves an 18 October inverse construction. Its supplied count-valued spectral clocks and separately excited response modes are mathematical comparison models. They are not a realization of the current proposal of C portions sharing one fundamental frequency, whose additive average registration rate is C times that fundamental. Persistence and response conclusions below apply only to the action and domains actually written here; they do not transfer to a different action. The current particle-geometry account develops that distinction and the newer constructions.

Two classes of effective actions extend the constructive count clocks. The first now has a nonlinear persistence theorem for its entire finite spatial dynamics, including current, independent profiles and responding material geometry. The second accommodates several different supplied clocks in one positive linear action, despite overlap of their actual spatial sources. Its alternative kinetic and response laws have different physical content. These results do not combine into an unwritten master action.

The spatial dimensions are ordinary directions in the shared physical space, taken here as R10\mathbb R^{10}R10. Real field components, profile coefficients and response coordinates describe Ψ∞\Psi_\inftyΨ∞​; they are neither extra spatial dimensions nor mediator particles. Field-norm localization is distinct from a position-probability law. In particular, none of these internal field constructions replaces the electron's literal deterministic external trajectory. Finite normal envelopes are supplied in both constructions, rather than derived exact confinement to a lower-dimensional layer.

Evidence and physical scope

The nonlinear result has 6,708 original-construction checks and 6,336 independent-construction checks, each replayed unchanged. A separate 1,883-check governing comparison verifies rational radical enclosures, off-reference four-profile measures and sparse occupations at distant shells, including J=1000,10000J=1000,10000J=1000,10000, as well as the localization bound. A further 38-check bounded verification supports the spatial and phase estimates. These are finite mathematical diagnostics supporting the analytic proof; they are not time integration, observed lifetimes or an infinite-band simulation.

The response constructions have 509 original and 343 independent checks, replayed unchanged, plus a separate replayed 122-check governing comparison. The latter includes a singular-source polar witness, complementary-mode identities and physical A0A_0A0​ source derivatives. Raw-density and normalized-source examples remain separate. The rank-six fourteen-column polar theorem uses its analytic square-root construction; no numerical fourteen-dimensional radical diagonalization is claimed.

The standalone spatial checker and its dated results contain the independent 6,336-check certificate. Its sufficient leakage basin differs from the governing moment basin (7)–(13); it must not be advertised as executing the governing 1,883 checks or the original 6,708. The response checker and results contain the independent 343-check construction. The provenance record distinguishes those copies from the original and governing evidence and pins the exact source versions.

Together these are stronger compatibility results at all maintained depths, including six and ten. They provide a finite nonlinear spatial persistence theorem and positive simultaneous linear response actions under explicit supplied data. They do not experimentally favor those depths, select observed occupations or sector units, infer lifetimes, derive electric charge or spin, establish photon or bottom mechanisms, or complete the physical mass operator. In particular, the response construction's prescribed templates have not been made autonomous localized solutions by the separate persistence theorem. The origin of the material connection, kinetic repairs and inverse response law remains a physical derivation problem.
